definitions.definition: A specified family of axiom instances generated from formula or term parameters.
definitions.name: Axiom schema

source_refs.locator: Definition int.6: a parameterized induction family; general schema convention

definitions.definition: A finite exploration of stated proof rules under explicit budgets. Exhaustion does not establish unprovability.
definitions.name: Bounded proof search

definitions.definition: Replace free occurrences of a variable; rename conflicting binders to preserve the binding of every other occurrence.
definitions.name: Capture-avoiding substitution

source_refs.locator: Section 2.4 and Section 5.1, rebinding during substitution

definitions.definition: The theory uses classical first-order logic with equality and an effective proof calculus when effectiveness is required. This is not inferred from a user-chosen theory name.
definitions.name: Classical first-order setting

definitions.definition: An extension adding no new theorems formulated in the original language.
definitions.name: Conservative extension

source_refs.locator: Section 2.7, Theorem 27A and 27D, no additional original-language consequences

definitions.definition: A classical theory T is consistent when it has no derivation of a contradiction, equivalently no sentence A for which it derives both A and not A. An input flag declaring this property is an assumption; software tests cannot certify it.
definitions.name: Syntactic consistency

definitions.definition: Con_Pr := not Pr(nu(code(bottom))); the chosen contradiction and provability predicate must be fixed.
definitions.name: Predicate-specific consistency formula

definitions.definition: For each sentence A: if T proves A then T proves Pr(nu(code(A))).
definitions.name: D1 derivability condition

definitions.definition: For every sentence pair A,B: T proves Pr(nu(code(A->B))) -> (Pr(nu(code(A)))->Pr(nu(code(B)))).
definitions.name: D2 derivability condition

definitions.definition: For every sentence A: T proves Pr(nu(code(A))) -> Pr(nu(code(Pr(nu(code(A)))))).
definitions.name: D3 derivability condition

definitions.definition: The particular axiom set of T has an algorithm that halts and decides membership for every candidate sentence. This condition concerns the supplied presentation, not decidability of all theorems.
definitions.name: Decidable axiom presentation

source_refs.locator: Section 4, printed p.10: recursive axiom sets are expressible; DecidableSet on p.9 is only proposition-level decidability

definitions.definition: A formula built from arithmetic atoms using connectives and bounded quantifiers. In each bound Qx<t, the term t does not contain x; bounded syntax is an abbreviation with a stated expansion.
definitions.name: Bounded arithmetic formula

source_refs.locator: Section 3.3, Theorem 33I, pp.210-211; library syntactic bounded-formula convention

definitions.definition: For every arithmetic formula theta(x) with at most x free there is a sentence D such that T proves D iff theta(code(D)), using the same syntax coding as its provability predicate.
definitions.name: Fixed-point lemma available

definitions.definition: An effective axiom presentation enumerates axioms by an algorithm. Decidable axiom membership is a stronger presentation condition. The associated proof relation must encode any required enumeration witnesses; different presentations can produce different internal provability predicates.
definitions.name: Effective axiomatization

source_refs.locator: Section 4: decidable axioms and representability requirements

definitions.definition: Syntax has a computable coding with decidable well-formedness, and the chosen classical calculus supports effective enumeration of finite derivations from an effective axiom presentation.
definitions.name: Effective syntax and proof enumeration

definitions.definition: A theory is essentially undecidable if every consistent extension in its language has an undecidable theorem set.
definitions.name: Essential undecidability

source_refs.locator: Section 3.5, Theorem 35C, hereditary undecidability for consistent extensions

definitions.definition: Every axiom of first-order PA is provable in T in the same arithmetic language. This is an explicit mathematical assumption, not inferred from the label PA.
definitions.name: Extension of PA

definitions.definition: A nonempty finite carrier with total functions, constants and relations interpreting a fixed signature.
definitions.name: Finite structure

definitions.definition: For one-variable A(x), a sentence G with T proving G iff A(nu(code(G))); this is provable equivalence, not literal text equality.
definitions.name: Sentence fixed point

definitions.definition: Con_Pr(T) abbreviates not Pr_T(code(0 = S0)) for the explicitly fixed provability predicate. Its intended interpretation and unprovability depend on that representation. No finite collection of successful proof checks establishes Con_Pr(T).
definitions.name: Consistency sentence relative to a predicate

definitions.definition: An atomic relation or equality, or an expression built with logical connectives and quantifiers.
definitions.name: Formula

definitions.definition: The least normal modal logic extending classical propositional logic by K and Box(Box A->A)->Box A, closed under modus ponens, necessitation and uniform substitution.
definitions.name: Goedel-Loeb modal logic

source_refs.locator: Section 3, axiomatic calculus K plus GL and necessitation

definitions.definition: For one fixed arithmetic formula Pr_T(x), and all arithmetic sentences A and B: D1, if T proves A then T proves Pr_T(code(A)); D2, T proves Pr_T(code(A -> B)) -> (Pr_T(code(A)) -> Pr_T(code(B))); D3, T proves Pr_T(code(A)) -> Pr_T(code(Pr_T(code(A)))). Numerals are implicit inside each coded formula. D1 is a metatheoretic rule; D2 and D3 are internal schemes.
definitions.name: Hilbert-Bernays-Loeb conditions

definitions.definition: A nonempty set of worlds with a binary accessibility relation; valuations turn a frame into a model.
definitions.name: Kripke frame

source_refs.locator: Section 2.1, relational models and nonempty frames

definitions.definition: Box A holds at a world iff A holds at every accessible successor, including vacuous truth when there are none.
definitions.name: Box semantics

definitions.definition: An injective assignment of natural numbers to finite syntactic presentations. Distinct presentations may denote the same formula.
definitions.name: Presentation-sensitive numbering

source_refs.locator: Section art.1; presentation sensitivity is a library convention, not a claim about its specific coding

definitions.definition: A closed arithmetic term denoting a specified natural number; this package documents an exact binary Horner convention.
definitions.name: Numeral term

source_refs.locator: Section 2.8, natToTerm; binary Horner is the library convention replacing unary notation

definitions.definition: For a total function f:N^k->N, R strongly represents f numeralwise in T when every standard input tuple a has T proving forall y(R(nu(a),y) iff y=nu(f(a))).
definitions.name: Numeralwise function representation

definitions.definition: Object formulas belong to a theory language. Metatheoretic assertions about derivability or consistency are distinct from object formulas arithmetizing them.
definitions.name: Object and metatheory levels

definitions.definition: There is no arithmetic formula phi(x), with x its only free variable, for which T proves exists x phi(x) and proves not phi(n) for every standard numeral n. This is a metatheoretic quantification over all standard numerals, not a bounded test.
definitions.name: Omega-consistency

source_refs.locator: Definition 2.1, with phi replaced by its negation

definitions.definition: In this catalogue 1-consistency means omega-consistency restricted to bounded arithmetic formulas. Over PA this is equivalent to Sigma-1 soundness. Authors' conventions differ; no unqualified one_consistent flag is accepted as a substitute for a theorem's sigma1_sound requirement.
definitions.name: Convention for 1-consistency

definitions.definition: Here one-consistency for a Q-extending arithmetic theory means no false Sigma1 sentence is provable. The convention is explicit.
definitions.name: One-consistency convention

source_refs.locator: Introduction and Definition 2.1; Sigma1-soundness is explicitly the library convention for one-consistency

definitions.definition: For every arithmetic A(x,parameters): (A(0) and forall x(A(x)->A(Sx))) -> forall x A(x), with parameter closure.
definitions.name: PA induction schema

definitions.definition: Use the same arithmetic language as Q. PA has the six successor/addition/multiplication axioms of Q and the universal closure of every induction instance (phi(0) and forall x (phi(x) -> phi(Sx))) -> forall x phi(x), with parameters allowed. PA proves the predecessor axiom. It is first-order PA, not full second-order arithmetic.
definitions.name: First-order Peano arithmetic PA

source_refs.locator: Section 2.8: PA axioms and induction scheme

definitions.definition: Here a syntactic Pi1 formula is a universal prefix followed by a bounded arithmetic matrix. Equivalence over PA to that form requires a separate justification.
definitions.name: Pi-one arithmetic formula

source_refs.locator: Section 3.5, arithmetical hierarchy, pp.242-243; library syntactic normal-form convention

definitions.definition: Obtained from zero, successor and projections by composition and primitive recursion.
definitions.name: Primitive recursive function

definitions.definition: Proof_T(p,x) arithmetically represents a specified proof relation, with fixed numbering, axioms and inference rules. It concerns arbitrary finite proofs, not only those below an implementation budget.
definitions.name: Arithmetized proof relation

source_refs.locator: Sections art.6-art.8; Propositions art.17, art.24, art.28

definitions.definition: Pr_T(x) := exists p Proof_T(p,x); its representation is part of its identity.
definitions.name: Provability formula

definitions.definition: A single arithmetic formula Pr_T and a single coding convention have been selected and are used consistently in HBL conditions and the displayed consistency/reflection sentence.
definitions.name: Fixed provability representation

definitions.definition: Robinson Q in the signature {0,S,+,*} has seven axioms: successor injectivity and nonzero values, predecessor for nonzero elements, and the four recursion equations for addition and multiplication. It has no induction schema.
definitions.name: Robinson arithmetic Q

source_refs.locator: Definition int.5: Q1-Q7 in the reduct without the separately definable order symbol; Q8 is a definition

definitions.definition: A set for which an effective procedure lists exactly its members; nonmembership need not be decidable.
definitions.name: Computably enumerable set

definitions.definition: A conditional implication Con(S)->Con(T), established in a stated metatheory; it does not assert either antecedent or consequent outright.
definitions.name: Relative consistency

source_refs.locator: Section 2.7, interpretation and model translation; conditional metatheoretic convention

definitions.definition: Classical first-order arithmetic with equality, 0, S, + and multiplication. Its seven universally closed axioms are: Sx != 0; Sx = Sy -> x = y; x != 0 -> exists y (x = Sy); x + 0 = x; x + Sy = S(x + y); x * 0 = 0; x * Sy = (x * y) + x. There is no induction scheme. This profile is descriptive; the package does not enumerate its axioms or decide its consistency.
definitions.name: Robinson arithmetic Q

definitions.definition: M,s |= A relates an interpreted structure M, a variable assignment s and a formula A.
definitions.name: Satisfaction

definitions.definition: For sentences Gamma and A, Gamma |= A means every structure satisfying Gamma satisfies A. For open formulas the local consequence convention additionally quantifies over the same variable assignment.
definitions.name: Semantic entailment

source_refs.locator: Definition syn.64 (sentences); local open-formula extension explicitly declared

definitions.definition: A formula whose set of free variables is empty.
definitions.name: Sentence

definitions.definition: Every Sigma-1 sentence proved by T is true in the standard natural numbers. Sigma-1 means an existential block over a formula with only bounded quantifiers, allowing the usual arithmetic equivalents. For the arithmetic theories used here this entails consistency.
definitions.name: Sigma-1 soundness

definitions.definition: An existential prefix followed by a bounded arithmetic matrix; PA-equivalence to this form must be justified separately.
definitions.name: Sigma-one arithmetic formula

source_refs.locator: Section 5, existential unbounded quantifiers in represented arithmetic relations; library syntactic normal-form convention

definitions.definition: Symbols with fixed arities; logical equality is distinguished from nonlogical predicates.
definitions.name: Formal signature

definitions.definition: A fixed effective coding of arithmetic syntax and finite proofs with a correctly represented proof relation and substitution operation in PA, and its usual Sigma-1 provability formula Pr_T. Catalogue claims use this mathematical convention. The package's finite JSON byte numbering is not asserted to supply a PA representation of its native checker.
definitions.name: Standard proof arithmetization

definitions.definition: The semantic structure is the standard natural numbers with their usual arithmetic operations. This stipulates an interpretation; the library does not decide truth in it.
definitions.name: Standard natural-number interpretation

definitions.definition: For each closed sentence A in the language of T, T proves A or proves not A. With consistency, exactly one alternative holds. This does not mean that every formula is true in every model.
definitions.name: Syntactic completeness

definitions.definition: A finite expression inductively formed from variables, constants and function applications.
definitions.name: Term

definitions.definition: An interpretation specifies a definable nonempty domain and translations preserving logical rules, functions and equality, such that the target theory proves translations of source axioms.
definitions.name: Interpretation between theories

definitions.definition: Truth N |= A is evaluated in the intended structure of natural numbers from a metatheory. Derivability T |- A is the existence of a finite derivation from T. They are distinct notions; classical first-order semantic completeness of a calculus does not say that PA decides every sentence.
definitions.name: Truth and provability
